Share county counts across smaller Census areas

Source: R/extrapolate_from_county.R
extrapolate_from_county.Rd

extrapolate_from_county() shares each county's count across the county's census tracts or block groups, in proportion to each area's population in the same stratum, from the American Community Survey (ACS) 5-year estimates. Run it on county data that has been through impute_suppressed().

The estimates are modelled, not observed: they assume the same rate in every area of a county within a stratum.

Usage

extrapolate_from_county(
  x,
  to = c("tract", "block group"),
  no_county = c("report", "spread"),
  spread_by = c("population", "cases"),
  empty_strata = c("total", "equal", "none"),
  ages = c("auto", "13+", "all"),
  race_table = c("B03002", "B01001"),
  unknown_race = c("report", "redistribute"),
  unestimated = c("leave out", "error"),
  acs_year = NULL,
  weights = NULL
)

Arguments

x

County data from get_atlas() that has been through impute_suppressed(), with at most one stratification variable.

to

The areas to share county counts across. Both nest inside counties, so the estimates add up to the county counts exactly:

  • "tract" (default): census tracts. ACS 5-year estimates from 2009.

  • "block group": census block groups. ACS 5-year estimates from 2013; smaller areas have larger ACS margins of error.

Areas that cross county lines, such as ZCTAs, are not supported yet.

no_county

Cases in state totals with no county (see no_county_cases()):

  • "report" (default): left out of the estimates, with a message giving the total. The report is kept in attr(result, "no_county_cases").

  • "spread": shared across the state's counties in x by their ACS population in the same stratum, then across areas as usual. Negative remainders are not spread, nor are remainders in a state with no allocated county in that stratum; the message says how many cases could not be spread.

spread_by

How no_county = "spread" shares a state's remainder among its counties:

  • "population" (default): by each county's ACS population in the stratum, as if cases with no county lived anywhere in the state.

  • "cases": in proportion to each county's own count in the stratum, as if cases with no county resembled cases with one. A state stratum with no county cases falls back to population.

Ignored for no_county = "report".

empty_strata

What to do when CDC reports cases in a county stratum but no area in the county has ACS population in it (for example a small county with no residents of one age group):

  • "total" (default): share by the areas' total population.

  • "equal": share equally across the county's areas.

  • "none": leave the estimates NA, with a warning.

ages

Ages the Census populations cover:

  • "auto" (default): 13 and older for HIV indicators (as CDC reports them), all ages otherwise.

  • "13+" or "all": set it yourself.

When x is stratified by age, the age groups set the ages, so 13 and older is used for the total population (the "total" fallback for empty strata).

race_table

The ACS table for race populations, used when x is stratified by race:

  • "B03002" (default): Hispanic or Latino origin by race. Its groups match AtlasPlus exactly (Hispanic, and non-Hispanic for each race), but it has no ages, so for ages 13 and older each area's populations are scaled by the area's share of residents aged 13 and older.

  • "B01001": the sex-by-age tables for each race (B01001B to B01001I), which give ages 13 and older directly. Only White (B01001H) and Hispanic (B01001I) match AtlasPlus; the other groups include Hispanic people of that race.

unknown_race

Cases CDC reports with race "Unknown", when x is stratified by race:

  • "report" (default): left out, with a message, and listed in attr(result, "not_allocated").

  • "redistribute": shared across the county's known race groups in proportion to their counts, within each indicator and year, then across areas as usual. A county with no cases of known race keeps its unknown cases unallocated.

unestimated

Suppressed rows impute_suppressed() couldn't estimate (cases_source = "not estimated", with no count), such as a county CDC still lists after it was abolished:

  • "leave out" (default): left out, with a message naming the counties, and listed in attr(result, "not_allocated"). Their cases count towards the state's remainder with no county.

  • "error": stop with an error.

acs_year

The last year of the ACS 5-year estimates. NULL (default) uses each data year. A single year can be given only if x has one year.

weights

Not yet supported; for sub-county weights later (#1).

Value

A tibble with one row per area, indicator, year and stratum:

year, acs_year

Data year and ACS year used.

area_type, geoid, area_name

to, and the area's Census GEOID and name.

county_fips, county_name, state_fips

The county and state the area is in.

indicator, race_ethnicity, sex, age, data_status

From x.

county_cases, cases_source, county_population_atlas

The county's count, where it came from (see impute_suppressed()) and CDC's county population.

county_cases_spread

Cases with no county added to this county (no_county = "spread"); 0 otherwise.

county_cases_unknown

Cases of unknown race added to this race group (unknown_race = "redistribute"); 0 otherwise.

county_cases_allocated

county_cases + county_cases_spread + county_cases_unknown: what the county's areas add up to.

area_population_acs, county_population_acs

ACS population in the stratum, for the area and the sum of the county's areas.

area_total_population, county_total_population

The same for the whole population at the same ages.

allocation

How the county's count was shared: "stratum population", "total population", "equal shares" or "none" (see empty_strata).

area_cases

Estimated cases in the area.

area_noncases

area_population_acs - area_cases, floored at 0.

Two attributes record what was not allocated: attr(result, "no_county_cases"), the no_county_cases() report, and attr(result, "not_allocated"), county rows left out, with a reason.

Details

The denominator is the sum of the county's areas, so the estimates add up to county_cases_allocated in every county stratum.

Census populations come from ACS tables requested by variable code: B01001 (sex by age) for all ages, sex and age, and for race the table set by race_table. For ages 13 and older, 2/5 of the 10 to 14 band is counted, assuming ages are spread evenly within it.

County rows with no Census denominator are left out and listed in attr(result, "not_allocated"): race "Other", race "Unknown" (unless redistributed), age groups other than CDC's HIV age groups, suppressed rows with no estimate (see unestimated), rows kept by impute_suppressed(not_available = "keep"), and counties with no ACS areas (such as Connecticut's planning regions with 2010 tracts, until #30 adds a crosswalk).

Tract and block group boundaries change every ten years, so estimates from ACS years on different sides of a decennial census (2017 and 2022, say) can't be compared area by area.

Needs the tidycensus package and a Census API key in the CENSUS_API_KEY environment variable (see tidycensus::census_api_key()). Also downloads the matching state data from CDC AtlasPlus for the no-county report.

Age-stratified extrapolation supports only HIV diagnoses and prevalence, because CDC's age groups for other diseases aren't matched to Census ages yet.

See also

impute_suppressed(), no_county_cases().

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
county <- get_atlas("hiv", "county", 2022, stratify_by = "sex")
county <- impute_suppressed(county)
tracts <- extrapolate_from_county(county)
block_groups <- extrapolate_from_county(county, to = "block group")

# Cases left out because they have no county
attr(tracts, "no_county_cases")
} # }
